assessment: Cultivation variability across the 12 scoped experiments is low for replicate pairs in nine of twelve experiments (peak offline VCD within +/-6.80 percent between R01 and R02; tightest fed-batch pair EXP010 -0.62 percent) and concentrates in three pairs with different characters: EXP001 (+64.90 percent, a growth-phase divergence - R01 peaked at 14000000 cells/mL at 136 h and crashed terminally to 0.28 percent viability, while R02 peaked at 8490000 cells/mL at 184 h, dipped mid-run and survived), EXP004 (+12.67 percent, moderate growth-phase difference plus a late-decline ammonium gap at the final sample), and EXP011 (+224.36 percent, a viability-specific collapse of R02). The EXP011/R02 collapse began between elapsed 51 h (viability 90.783 percent) and 67 h (38.47 percent): viable cell density fell to zero by 148.5 h while total cell density stayed near 5706667 cells/mL, inline permittivity independently corroborates the collapse (peaks +92.95 percent apart and tracking in time), ammonium rose to 48.934 mM, and glucose fell to 0.994 g/L at its last recorded assay (67 h). Specialist review localized the associated input discontinuities: the R02 feed log ENDS at its final row (11.42 g at 67.139 h, cell verified) while the process-parameter log continues to 195.6 h; NaOH never exceeds 1.74 g (R01 55.79 g, still step-increasing at its final row) and stops rising by about 95 h with its log continuing; O2 enrichment reads 0.0 from 66.983 h while pH stays 7.014-7.066 and DO 3.06-11.97 percent air sat. Whether feed delivery physically stopped, was stopped intentionally, or only its recording stopped cannot be determined from the scoped package (no controller, recipe or event-log evidence), so causation remains open with competing hypotheses. The EXP001 divergence remains partly unexplained because inline permittivity (+3.19 percent) and turbidity (-1.35 percent) peaks agree while offline TCD/VCD peaks differ +44.36/+64.90 percent - a measurement-contribution question that raw replicate data or an independent biomass assay would resolve. Recording-integrity findings (no cultivation impact): a duplicated ~1 h clock window in EXP004 (file-level, 0.9917 h backwards seam step), single 30-second out-of-order records in EXP007/R02 and EXP012/R02, constant-zero dead permittivity channels on EXP001-EXP003 R02 sheets, fixed 100 rpm setpoints in EXP008-EXP012, zero feed in all batch workbooks, a mid-run DO sag to 1.6 percent in EXP005/R01, a 4-minute optical reflection transient in EXP001 (both runs), on-demand aeration channels reading 0 at final records, and repeated trailing rows in several sheets. No proven cause is established for any divergence; severity is an advisory proposal pending the configured routing policy, and all disposition decisions remain with human review.
cross_scope_synthesis: Shared patterns: (1) All 12 workbooks share the same 8-sheet run structure with elapsed-hours clocks, so replicates are directly comparable; nine of twelve pairs agree within +/-6.80 percent on peak offline VCD, and every experiment shows a late-culture viability decline at the final samples - expected batch/fed-batch end-of-run behavior rather than distinctive faults. (2) The material variability signals differ in kind: EXP001 is growth-phase (both offline count channels move together; inline proxies agree), EXP004 is moderate growth-phase plus a final-sample ammonium gap, and EXP011 is viability-specific (TCD peaks agree within -6.23 percent while VCD peaks differ +224.36 percent; dead-cell mass persists; inline permittivity corroborates). (3) The EXP011/R02 input discontinuities cluster tightly in time (feed log ends 67.139 h; O2 enrichment 0 from 66.983 h; viability collapse between 51 and 67 h; glucose last assay 0.994 g/L at 67 h) while pH/DO/temperature/agitation logs continue in narrow bands - consistent with either a real process event around 67 h or a coupled recording discontinuity; the scoped data cannot discriminate. (4) Recording-integrity signals recur across sources and are best explained as acquisition/export artifacts: duplicated clock windows (EXP004, file-level), single out-of-order records (EXP007/R02, EXP012/R02), dead/not-populated multi-frequency permittivity channels on EXP001-EXP003 R02 sheets (Status stays Ok), repeated trailing rows, and endpoint zeros on on-demand gas channels. (5) Design-level differences separate the workbook groups: batch runs (EXP001-EXP009) record zero feed throughout and EXP001-EXP007 use variable agitation while EXP008-EXP012 hold a fixed 100 rpm setpoint; fed-batch runs (EXP010-EXP012) record feed and reach the highest densities (EXP010 ~16.1 million cells/mL with osmolality 511 vs 510). Exceptions: EXP011/R02 is the only run with a truncated feed log, discontinued glucose/lactate assays and a whole-run viability collapse; EXP001 is the only batch pair with a certified growth divergence above 60 percent; EXP005/R01 carries the only mid-run DO sag to 1.6 percent air sat. Missing evidence: no recipe, controller, calibration, event-log, contamination or raw-replicate records are in the scoped package; reported offline Mean/SEM values are source summaries whose raw replicates are unavailable, so no independent-replicate SEM could be computed. Implications: pooled variability statistics should flag EXP001/R01-R02, EXP004 and EXP011/R02; inline-series timing analyses should avoid the flagged sheets until re-exported; and the EXP011 divergence should not be attributed to any cause without controller/event-log evidence.

interpretations.statement: EXP007/R02 clock flag is a single one-interval out-of-order record - a recording/export ordering artifact. There are no duplicated clock values and no value discontinuity; it does not indicate a process event or a clock reset. Screening shows single-step flags also on EXP007/R01 permittivity and turbidity sheets, so small out-of-order records recur in this file.

EXP004/R02 inline clock flags come from a duplicated clock window: a backwards step of about one hour at the seam (linked metrics) and a block of repeated clock values with slightly different measurements. Values stay physically plausible and show no step at the seam, so the flags are recording/acquisition artifacts (clock rewind/reset or overlapping export segments), not evidence of a process disturbance at the seam. Screening flags on EXP004/R01 and online sheets indicate the clock irregularity is file-wide; I verified the R02 inline seam only.

EXP012/R02 constant agitation is consistent with a fixed setpoint being recorded for the whole run; it matches the R01 replicate and every constant agitation series in EXP008-EXP012, and all sibling channels on the sheet are live. It is not a failed-sensor signature on its own; recipe/controller records would be needed to separate 'logged setpoint' from 'measured constant'.

EXP009/R01 and EXP008/R02 constant-zero cumulative feed weight is consistent with batch operation without feed: every batch-run series is constant at 0.0 g while the fed-batch runs record varying nonzero weights. It is an expected/ambiguous recording state rather than a failed sensor; recipe confirmation is missing.

EXP002/R02 and EXP003/R02 zero-peak channels are dead/not-populated channels, not real measurements: the multi-frequency and fit-output channels are exactly 0.0 for the entire run while Conductivity and Permittivity on the same sheets vary and the R01 counterparts are live. The paired peak comparisons therefore compare a live channel against a dead channel and are not evidence of a replicate process or biological difference. Simultaneous Fitting Error RMSE=0.0 and Fitting Quality R2=0.0 is internally inconsistent for a real Cole fit, supporting placeholder zeros. EXP001/R02 shares this pattern.

End-of-run declines (viability at low levels in the last recorded offline sample of nearly all runs, aeration rates falling to 0, lactate falling to 0.086 g/L at its last recorded value) are present across the package and are consistent with expected late-culture decline and run shutdown rather than distinctive process faults.

Replicate-run cultivation variability is small in most of the scoped package: nine of twelve R01/R02 pairs have peak offline VCD within +/-6.80 percent, and the tightest fed-batch pair (EXP010) differs by -0.62 percent. The variability signal is concentrated in EXP001, EXP004 and EXP011.

The EXP011/R02 signal is a viability-specific collapse, not a failure to grow: total cell density peaks differ only -6.23 percent while viable density peaks differ +224.36 percent, and inline permittivity peaks differ +92.95 percent and follow the offline collapse in time. Dead-cell mass remaining in the bioreactor is consistent with total cell density staying near 5706667 cells/mL while VCD went to zero.

In EXP011/R02 the recorded feed/NaOH interruption, glucose exhaustion (last recorded 0.994 g/L at 67 h) and the viability collapse cluster in the same 51-67 h window; ammonium accumulation to 48.934 mM followed the collapse, but the package contains no controller, recipe or event-log evidence that would discriminate between a feed-delivery stop, an intentional stop, a recording gap, or a biological cause.

EXP001 shows a growth-phase divergence between same-design replicates (R01 higher peak, earlier and terminal crash; R02 lower peak, mid-run viability dip with recovery). Medium chemistry was similar between the runs, so the package does not contain an input difference that explains it. However, inline permittivity peaks agree within +3.19 percent and inline turbidity maxima within -1.35 percent while offline TCD/VCD peaks differ +44.36/+64.90 percent, so a contribution from offline assay variability, timing or cell-morphology differences cannot be excluded.

EXP004 is a moderate, growth-phase variability case (VCD peak +12.67 percent, R02 peaking at elapsed hour 118 versus 142 in R01 at a lower value); its ammonium gap (+49.94 percent) arises at the elapsed-hour-212 sample (10.45 versus 6.86 mM) and not at hour 195 (7.25 versus 6.97 mM), during the shared decline phase.

EXP011/R02 feed discontinuity is a recording stop rather than a flatline inside a continuing log: the final row of R02_online_Feed is at elapsed 67.139 h (11.42 g) while the R02 process-parameter log continues to 195.6 h and the NaOH log to 195.167 h.

EXP011/R02 NaOH difference (1.74 g versus 55.79 g in R01) with pH never recorded below 7.014 is consistent with low acid demand from the collapsed culture rather than a base-delivery fault, but pump/controller evidence to discriminate is not in scope.

After the recorded feed end, EXP011/R02 pH and dissolved-O2 records stay inside narrow bands (pH 7.02-7.066; DO 3.06-11.97 percent air sat), so the scoped data contain no recorded pH excursion during the collapse; the low DO with O2 enrichment off remains unexplained.

The EXP011/R02 VCD and viability collapse (VCD 0 from elapsed 148.5 h) and the ammonium rise (48.93 mM, 4.42 times the R01 peak) occur after the recorded feed end at 67.139 h; temporal association does not establish causal direction.

EXP011/R02: why did ammonium accumulate to 48.934 mM - cause or consequence of the collapse?
EXP011/R02: why were glucose assays discontinued after 67 h and lactate assays after 148.5 h?

EXP001: why did the replicate growth trajectories diverge after roughly 91-115 h, and why do inline permittivity/turbidity peaks agree within about 3-4 percent while offline TCD/VCD peaks differ 44.36/64.90 percent?
EXP001: what is the physical cause of the reflection transients (4-minute optical events in both runs) and of the roughly tenfold larger turbidity scale versus other experiments?
EXP005/R01: what caused the mid-run DO sag to 1.6 percent air sat at 104.983 h with O2 enrichment peaking at 9.84 sL/h, and was it within intended control?

Are the reported offline Mean/SEM summaries based on enough raw replicates to support the variability conclusions, given raw replicate values are not in the scoped package?

EXP001-EXP003 R02 permittivity sheets: were the multi-frequency channels disabled, not exported, or hardware-failed while the Status field stayed Ok?
Do the Status columns of EXP002/R02 and EXP003/R02 permittivity sheets read Ok beyond their first 20 records?
EXP012/R02 inline permittivity shows one 30-second backwards step (row 1913) outside the assigned candidates - same out-of-order recording pattern, not yet row-verified.
Are the identical trailing final records (last three rows repeated in several ProcessParameters/turbidity sheets) steady state or an export tail artifact?
Do recipe/controller records confirm the fixed 100 rpm agitation setpoint (EXP008-EXP012) and the no-feed batch design (EXP001-EXP009)?
